newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief, Holzmann step up talks.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief, Holzmann step up talks.

text.p: German construction groups Philipp Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG have intensified their talks about cooperation despite a dispute over Hochtief's plan to increase its stake in Holzmann, Hochtief said on Tuesday.
"There were and still are talks about how one can cooperate," a Hochtief spokeswoman said. She said the talks were independent of the stake dispute between the two builders.
Hochtief is taking legal action aimed at overturning a veto by the Federal Cartel Office of its bid to raise its 20 percent stake in market leader Holzmann to 35 percent.
The Hochtief spokeswoman and the cartel office on Tuesday denied reports that an out-of-court settlement had been reached.
The spokeswoman said the cooperation talks had never been abandoned even at the height of the dispute. The firms had, for example, discussed the possibility of working together in foreign projects.
Driven by mounting pressure resulting from costs and competition, the two companies had intensified those talks but no concrete result had been reached yet, the spokeswoman said.
The first court hearing in the dispute is set for February 5 next year.
Hochtief launched its bid in 1994, arguing that the companies, both modestly sized by international standards, needed to merge to beat off international competition.

But the bid ran into trouble when the cartel office said a merger could create a monopoly position in the market for large projects. It also voiced concerns about the financial clout of Hochtief's owner, giant utility RWE AG.
Meanwhile Hochtief has parked two packages of Holzmann shares with an independent consultancy firm.
